receipt.public_excerpt: Within 30 days of the date of this order, the Attorney General shall establish an AI Litigation Task Force (Task Force) whose sole responsibility shall be to challenge State AI laws inconsistent with the policy set forth in section 2 of this order

evidence_items.explanation: The order does not void state AI laws. It sets up a task force to challenge them later in court, so existing state laws stayed on the books when Marcus wrote.

receipt.public_excerpt: A number of states have so far proposed or enacted legislation to regulate AI; in September and October, California, home to Silicon Valley, enacted significant AI regulations, including SB 53.

evidence_items.explanation: A same-day legal summary confirms that states, including California, had enacted significant AI regulations that were still on the books when the order was signed.

receipt.public_excerpt: SB 53 requires advanced AI developers to publish governance frameworks and transparency reports, establishes mechanisms for reporting critical safety incidents, extends whistleblower protections, and calls for the development of a public computing cluster.

evidence_items.explanation: California enacted a frontier AI safety law with real duties for developers less than three months before the post. That is not 'essentially zero' regulation.

receipt.public_excerpt: Until such a national standard exists, however, it is imperative that my Administration takes action to check the most onerous and excessive laws emerging from the States that threaten to stymie innovation.

evidence_items.explanation: The order itself treats state AI laws as existing and in force, and aims to 'check' them in the future. This supports Marcus's view of the order's aim, but not his claim of zero regulation.

unresolved_gaps: I did not set out a full list of state AI laws in force on 2025-12-12. Several, such as California SB 53 and Texas TRAIGA, took effect on 2026-01-01, after the post.
If 'essentially zero' was meant loosely, as 'very weak overall,' that is a judgment the evidence cannot settle.
